questions.question: Which structure controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell?
questions.explanation: The cell membrane is partially permeable and controls which substances enter or leave the cell.

questions.question: Which organelle releases energy from glucose during aerobic respiration?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration, releasing energy from glucose.

questions.question: A plant cell placed in distilled water becomes turgid. This is because

options.A: water leaves the cell by osmosis
options.B: water enters the cell by osmosis and the wall resists further expansion
options.C: the cytoplasm pulls away from the wall

questions.explanation: Water moves in by osmosis; the inelastic cell wall pushes back, making the cell firm (turgid) instead of bursting.

questions.question: Which pair of raw materials is needed for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water to make glucose, releasing oxygen.

questions.question: When testing a leaf for starch, it is boiled in ethanol in order to
questions.explanation: Boiling in ethanol removes chlorophyll so that the iodine colour change can be seen clearly.

questions.question: The optimum pH for the stomach enzyme pepsin is about
questions.explanation: Pepsin works best in the acidic conditions of the stomach, around pH 2.

questions.question: A deficiency of vitamin C causes
questions.explanation: Scurvy (bleeding gums, slow healing) is caused by lack of vitamin C; rickets is vitamin D deficiency.

questions.question: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart?
questions.explanation: The pulmonary vein is the only vein carrying oxygenated blood — from the lungs to the left atrium.

questions.question: Which is the word equation for aerobic respiration?

options.B: Glucose + oxygen to carbon dioxide + water + energy
options.C: Glucose to ethanol + carbon dioxide + energy
options.D: Carbon dioxide + water to glucose + oxygen

questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration needs oxygen and releases carbon dioxide, water and energy.

questions.question: Anaerobic respiration in yeast produces
questions.explanation: Yeast ferments glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide; muscles produce lactic acid instead.

questions.question: In a food chain, the producer is the organism that

options.B: captures light energy to make food

questions.explanation: Producers (green plants) convert light energy into chemical energy stored in food.

questions.question: Which group returns mineral nutrients from dead organisms to the soil?
questions.explanation: Decomposers (bacteria and fungi) break down dead matter, recycling nutrients into the soil.

questions.question: Which hormone lowers the blood glucose level?
questions.explanation: Insulin, secreted by the pancreas, lowers blood glucose by promoting its uptake and storage.

questions.question: Where does fertilisation take place in humans?
questions.explanation: Sperm meets the egg in the oviduct; the embryo then travels to implant in the uterus.

questions.question: Which of these diseases is caused by a virus?
questions.explanation: HIV/AIDS is viral; malaria is caused by Plasmodium (a protist), while cholera and TB are bacterial.

questions.question: Filtration of blood in the kidney happens in the
questions.explanation: High pressure in the glomerulus forces water, salts, glucose and urea into the Bowman's capsule.

questions.question: State TWO structural differences between a plant cell and an animal cell.
questions.answer: Plant cells have a cell wall and chloroplasts, which animal cells lack; plant cells have a large permanent vacuole while animal cells have only small temporary vacuoles.
questions.explanation: Accept any two: cell wall, chloroplasts, large permanent vacuole (plant only).

questions.question: A student increases light intensity but the rate of photosynthesis stops rising. Explain why.
questions.answer: Another factor, such as carbon dioxide concentration or temperature, has become the limiting factor.
questions.explanation: Once light is no longer limiting, whichever factor is in shortest supply caps the rate.

questions.question: Explain why an enzyme is denatured at high temperatures.
questions.answer: Heat breaks the bonds holding the enzyme's shape, so the active site changes shape and the substrate no longer fits.
questions.explanation: Denaturation is the loss of the specific 3D shape, so the enzyme-substrate complex cannot form.

questions.question: Explain TWO ways in which red blood cells are adapted to carry oxygen.
questions.answer: They are biconcave discs with a large surface area for diffusion; they have no nucleus, leaving more space for haemoglobin.
questions.explanation: Also accept: thin membrane for a short diffusion distance; haemoglobin binds oxygen.

questions.question: Define the term ecosystem.
questions.answer: A community of living organisms interacting with each other and their non-living environment.
questions.explanation: Must include both the living (biotic) and the non-living (abiotic) parts.

questions.question: State TWO methods of contraception.
questions.answer: Any two from: condom, contraceptive pill, injection, implant, intra-uterine device, abstinence.
questions.explanation: Accept any two recognised methods of contraception.

questions.question: State TWO uses of the energy released by respiration in the human body.
questions.answer: Any two from: muscle contraction, growth and cell division, maintaining body temperature, active transport.
questions.explanation: Respiration energy powers all energy-requiring processes in cells.

questions.question: State TWO ways by which cholera can be prevented.
questions.answer: Any two from: drinking clean or boiled water, proper sanitation and latrines, washing hands, cooking food thoroughly.
questions.explanation: Cholera spreads through contaminated water and food.
